When I became a manager, I had difficulty delegating. I wanted to do everything myself. That was a mistake. In my first year, my team had difficulty meeting deadlines, and I had difficulty sleeping. Then a mentor helped me to see the problem. She encouraged me to ask my team for ideas, not only for results. Now, every Monday, I encourage each analyst to share one problem and one solution. We help each other to find answers. Last quarter, a junior analyst had difficulty explaining a credit model to a client. I did not take the call for him. I helped him to prepare, and I encouraged him to lead the meeting. He did a great job. So my advice is simple. If people have difficulty doing something, do not do it for them. Help them to do it, and encourage them to try again.
